title: Clarify routing ordering and model-pinning behaviour during canary / A-B rollouts
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Background:
Redwood routing supports region selection, tier routing (by customer tier/capacity), and fallback model variants. We need explicit, implementation-grade rules for how model version pinning and progressive rollouts (canary / A-B) interact with these routing dimensions across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Current behavior has ambiguous ordering and a few production surprises (see incident notes in comments).

Goals:
- Define deterministic routing precedence: region -> pinning -> tier -> canary assignment -> fallback.
- Clarify semantics for: request-level pinning, session sticky pinning, customer-level pin overrides, and rollout percent evaluation order.
- Ensure consistent behavior across Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private deployments (document any environment-specific differences).
- Provide rollout tooling hooks (metrics, traces, opt-in/opt-out) and safe rollback paths.

Design decisions (proposed):
1) Precedence and evaluation order (deterministic):
   - Step 1: Region affinity evaluation (client region header / geo routing / customer preference). If region unavailable, go to configured region failover list.
   - Step 2: Model version pin check (explicit pin on request or customer config). If pinned and pinned model is available in chosen region and tier, route to that model variant. If pinned model is not available in region, consult pin_fallback policy: (a) fail-fast with a 409 and explanatory error if strict_pin=true, (b) else fall through to next step (recommended default).
   - Step 3: Tier routing by customer plan / capacity slab. Tier routing picks candidate pools within the selected region.
   - Step 4: Canary / A-B assignment: for unpinned requests, evaluate rollout policy percentages to map request to a variant. Assignment must be stateless per request (deterministic hashing by request id + customer id + rollout id) unless sticky sessions requested.
   - Step 5: Fallback chain: if chosen variant is unavailable (OOM, node failure, model missing), fallback to compatible variant list by decreasing fidelity (model-1.4 -> model-1.3 -> model-legacy) then to lower-tier variant or finally to region fallback.

2) Pinning semantics:
   - Request-level pin: header or param (x-redwood-model-pin) overrides rollout and tier selection for that request only.
   - Customer-level pin: tenant config in control plane that pins all requests unless request-level pin present. Customer pin is higher precedence than rollout but lower than region availability checks (see Step 2).
   - Session sticky pin: optional; if enabled, initial request participates in rollout assignment and the chosen variant is sticky for subsequent requests for the session_id for a TTL. Sticky mode must be opt-in (default OFF) and controlled by client SDK flags.

3) Canary / A-B rollout evaluation:
   - Percent-based assignment is done after tier routing so canaries are served within the same capacity pool as control.
   - Assignment uses a 64-bit hash of (rollout_id + customer_id + request_id) and maps fractional ranges to variants. This makes rollouts reproducible for replayable requests.
   - Admin console can opt to seed a whitelist of customer ids for exact targeting (100% deterministic).

4) Observability and safety:
   - Emit routing decision trace (region, tier, pin_source, rollout_id, variant_id, fallback_reason) for every request.
   - Expose per-variant SLO metrics: latency_p50/95/99, error_rate, generation_quality_score (from eval harness).
   - Auto-rollback hooks: if variant error_rate > configured threshold OR quality regression > delta for N minutes, mark canary unhealthy and automatically divert traffic to control and create a rollback ticket.

5) API and console changes required:
   - API: support x-redwood-model-pin header and pin_fallback query param. Document HTTP 409 behavior for strict pin.
   - Console: rollout UI to define rollout_id, variant weights, target regions, whitelist customers, sticky flag, and pin_fallback policy. Show live traffic percentages and per-variant metrics.

6) Dedicated and Private considerations:
   - Dedicated: rollout assignment must respect reserved capacity quotas; canary percentages should be translated into slot reservations when needed (avoid noisy neighbor impacts).
   - Private (on-prem): Control-plane features (rollout decisions) are optional. If control-plane unavailable, clients should be able to provide local rollout configuration bundles. Document delta in behavior and failure modes.

Migration / Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (2 sprints): Implement deterministic evaluation order and tracing for Hosted runtime. Add support for x-redwood-model-pin and pin_fallback behavior.
- Phase 2 (2 sprints): Canary assignment hashing library + console rollout UI. Hook up metrics/alerts for auto-rollback.
- Phase 3 (2 sprints): Dedicated capacity integration & quota mapping. Private deployment client-side rollout bundles + docs.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Should customer-level pinning be visible to end users via an API? (privacy/ops concerns)
- Default pin_fallback behavior: currently proposing fall-through (safer availability). Some teams prefer strict_pin to avoid silent model mismatches.
- Sticky session TTL defaults: 10 minutes vs session-oriented semantics.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit and integration tests cover ordering semantics and pin_fallback permutations.
- E2E test that simulates region outage and verifies pin_fallback behavior.
- Console can define rollout with region-level constraints and show live metrics.
- Metrics-based auto-rollback triggers that have been exercised in a staging canary.

Related artifacts:
- Design doc: https://drive.redwood/company/design/smart-routing/pinning-rollouts-draft (internal)
- Staging PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2894
- Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood/s/dashboards/rollouts/ENG-9347

Next steps:
- (Alex) Draft server-side routing precedence unit tests and attach to PR.
- (Priya) Coordinate with PM (Maya Rivera) to confirm default pin_fallback policy and communicate with customers with active pins.
- (SRE) Add canary alert playbook for auto-rollback behavior.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Alex Chen: Ran a short experiment in staging that showed canary percentage evaluated before tier routing — caused uneven capacity usage. Updating design to evaluate rollout after tier routing.
2025-02-18 - Maya Rivera (PM): Agree with fall-through default for pin_fallback. Customers with strict regulatory needs should set strict_pin and be documented. I'll update the PRD.

2025-02-22 - Samir Patel (SRE): Noted an incident where pinned model was deployed only to us-west-2 — we briefly returned 409s for EU requests. Recommend adding region-aware pin deployment checks in the control plane.
2025-03-03 - Design review (Lina Morales): Console mockups look good; please include a visible badge when a customer is pinned to a non-default model to avoid confusion in support.
2025-03-05 - Alex Chen: Added initial tracing fields to runtime and pushed staging PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2894. Need review from runtime team (cc: @runtime-eng).
